_comment: The current targeting snapshot, loaded by `manage.py targeting_import --from-manifest`. Rebuilding this dataset from source costs 30-45 minutes of API calls and can exhaust WorldPop's daily quota for everyone else, so a new environment should restore from here rather than re-fetch. Pin a new drive_file_id whenever the dataset changes materially: export, upload to the folder below (shared with connect-labs-sa), and update the id, created_at and counts in one commit so the file and the record stay together.
notes:
Restore with: make manage CMD="targeting_import --from-manifest --prune". USE --prune: these snapshots are authoritative rather than additive, and an un-pruned restore leaves superseded arithmetic behind (see derive.sweep_derived). Needs LABS_SYNTHETIC_GDRIVE_SA_KEY, already in the ECS task definition. 

160,569 values across 104 indicators, against 122,885 / 69 earlier the same day. Tiers 1 and 2 of docs/targeting-data-acquisition.md. 

TIER 1 -- twenty DHS indicators that had always been published subnationally and were never requested. We load 25 of DHS's 4,655, and the gaps fell along whole intervention categories rather than geography: family planning could not be targeted at all, nor zero-dose immunisation (the quantity immunisation funding is allocated against, not implied by DPT3), nor anaemia, nor the difference between a family that never reached care and one that reached it and was sent away untreated. 9,039 values, 29-41 countries each. Validated by weighted rollup: Liberia care-seeking 66.6% vs a published 65-70%, Nigeria severe wasting 1.7% vs 2-3%, Kenya zero-dose 3.9% vs low single digits. 

TIER 2 -- UNICEF's subnational SDMX, to reach countries DHS never surveyed. MICS proper is NOT reachable (per-survey SPSS microdata behind registration); the JMP's WASH_HOUSEHOLD_SUBNAT is the harmonised form and pools DHS, MICS, MIS and national surveys. WASH goes 38 -> 43 countries; neonatal mortality 30.7% -> 43.3% of ADM1 and 40% -> 71.3% of ADM2. Gain is five countries, not the eight first estimated: Egypt publishes to survey analysis regions and Algeria to programme zones, neither of which joins our governorate/wilaya boundaries, and the matcher refused both rather than guessing. 

TRAP RECORDED: UNICEF mixes tessellations WITHIN a country. Tunisia carries seven economic regions from MICS 2018 and a few governorates from MICS 2012; taking the latest observation per AREA kept both, our names matched only the governorates -- three of the four being the poorest interior ones -- and the country rolled up to 14.5% open defecation against a true figure near zero. Partial matching does not leave a gap, it produces a biased number that looks complete. One series is now held per country. 

Research notes are NOT in this snapshot -- they live in git and are written by `manage.py seed_targeting_research`, which should be run after any import.
